name: PLABench
description: Leakage-controlled, target-centric benchmark of protein-ligand binding affinity prediction: Davis and KIBA under warm, cold-target and cold-drug splits, CASP16 ligand series L1000 and L3000, and a ChEMBL35 test set filtered against the training data of the evaluated models.

attributes.task: Protein-ligand binding affinity prediction and target-centric ligand ranking
attributes.scope_note: Tables 2-4 extracted. Figure-only analyses (input pose accuracy ladder, interaction counts, per-target Kendall tau) not extracted.

name: Boltz2 (CASP16 and ChEMBL35 evaluation, PLABench)
description: Boltz2 as evaluated in PLABench (structure-based).

attributes.parameters: Published checkpoint applied without retraining; co-folds its own complex from sequence and SMILES, so the supplied structures are not consumed. 10 structural samples, affinity scored on the highest-ipTM pose, 500 sampling steps, 5 recycling steps (Methods lines 437-439)
attributes.access_reuse: Not stated per model in the source; see each model's release

name: PLABench CASP16 L1000 affinity
description: Affinity prediction on CASP16 series L1000; structure-based models given the same AlphaFold3-predicted complex structures.

attributes.protocol: CASP16 L1000 series; MSE, RMSE, Pearson, Spearman, rm2 and CI as printed in Table 3
limitations: Each series is a single target; Figure 2 states that each tau is computed over all ligands of a series, and Methods define the metrics over all test pairs.
Only one value per cell is printed; no uncertainty is reported in Tables 2-4.
Structure-based models received AlphaFold3-predicted structures, not crystal structures (Results).
Affinities in this series have a narrow high-affinity range, which the authors note makes RMSE and ranking metrics disagree.
